problem.text: What is the smallest positive integer $n$ such that $2016n$ is a perfect cube?

steps.title: Where to start: a cube has exponents divisible by $3$
steps.body: A positive integer is a perfect cube exactly when every prime in its factorization has an exponent that is a multiple of $3$. The question is about making $2016n$ a cube, so first factor $2016$ and look at its exponents.

steps.title: Add as little as possible to each exponent
steps.body: Multiplying by $n$ can only raise exponents. To keep $n$ small, $n$ should contain no primes other than $2$, $3$, $7$, and each exponent should be raised only up to the next multiple of $3$. For the prime $2$, the exponent $5$ goes up to $6$, so $n$ needs exactly one factor of $2$.

your_turn.prompt: How many factors of $3$ must $n$ supply, and why?
your_turn.answer: One: the exponent of $3$ in $2016$ is $2$, and the next multiple of $3$ is $3$.

steps.title: Now the prime $7$
steps.body: The exponent of $7$ in $2016$ is $1$, so it has to reach $3$, and $n$ must supply $7^2$. Careful: multiplying by just one $7$ is a common slip. It makes the exponent $2$, which is not a multiple of $3$.

your_turn.prompt: With $n$ supplying $2^1$, $3^1$ and $7^2$, what are the exponents of $2$, $3$ and $7$ in $2016n$?
